title: Source connector
description: C11 (draft): a source connector, a program the runner `ulei-connectors` starts on a schedule to pull new raw records of one source. Its directory in `connectors.dir` holds the `Manifest` as `connector.json`. Once per run the runner hands it a `Request`; the connector answers `Item`s with cursors over the transport its manifest names (`x-stdio`, `x-mcp`) or an `Error`. The runner puts each item into the archive as a C10 `put` with `source` set to the manifest's `name`; the connector never reaches the archive. Inside a run the connector reaches the network only through the broker (`BrokerRequest`, `BrokerReply`) unless the owner's `connectors.<name>.network` says otherwise. The runner appends one `RunRecord` per run to `connectors.log` (ADR-0056).

x-stdio.request: the runner writes the `Request` as one JSON line on stdin and closes it
x-stdio.lines: the connector writes one `Line` per line on stdout, UTF-8 JSON ended by a newline; the run's last line is `done` or `error`
x-stdio.stderr: free text for the run log
x-stdio.long_line: the runner reads at most `max_line_bytes` of a line and discards the rest; such an `item` counts as `too_large`

x-mcp.server: the connector is an MCP server over stdio, newline-delimited JSON-RPC, initialized with the protocol version and client info of the engine's MCP client (ADR-0026)
x-mcp.paging: the result's `structuredContent` is a `Page`; while `more` is true the runner calls again with the page's `cursor`; a result with `isError` carries an `Error` as `structuredContent`; a page delivers as its items followed by a `checkpoint` with its cursor

Name.description: A connector's name: its directory in `connectors.dir`, its item section in `ulei.toml` and the C10 `source` of its items. `dialogue` is the archive's own source and is no connector's name.

Semver.description: A semantic version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with an optional pre-release or build suffix.

HostPort.description: `host:port`: a DNS name, an IPv4 address or a bracketed IPv6 address, then a port.

Cursor.description: The connector's own position in its source, opaque to the runner, at most 4,096 bytes of UTF-8.

ExternalId.description: The source's id of a record, at most 512 bytes of UTF-8: C10 `put.external_id`.

Bytes.description: The original bytes in standard base64 with padding (RFC 4648 section 4): C10 `put.bytes_b64`.

Transport.description: `stdio`: the line protocol of `x-stdio`; `mcp`: an MCP server serving `ulei_pull` (`x-mcp`).

Schedule.description: When the connector is due: `every` seconds after its last start.

SourceAddresses.description: The network addresses of the source, the only ones the broker connects to without an owner record.

addresses.description: `host:port` entries; empty for a source that needs no network.

Manifest.description: `connector.json` in the connector's directory. It names no access beyond its source's addresses and its key: every widening is the owner's record in `ulei.toml`.

command.description: The argv; the program is a path relative to the connector's directory without a `..` segment, or an absolute path under `/usr`.

timeout.description: Seconds a run may take; default 300.

key.description: The name of the key the connector needs; the owner's `connectors.<name>.key_file` holds it. Absent, the connector reads no key.

Request.description: What the runner hands the connector once per run (stdio) or as the `ulei_pull` arguments of each page (MCP).

cursor.description: The last cursor the runner stored, at most 4,096 bytes; null on the first run and after `reset`.

limit.description: Items per page; the runner sends 100.

key_file.description: The absolute path of the key's env-file, the only key the run can read; null for a connector without `key`.

data_dir.description: The connector's own directory, the only one it may write.

Item.description: One raw record: C10 `PutRequest` without `source`, which only the runner sets. An item whose `put` body would exceed C10's 1,048,576 bytes is not sent and counts as `too_large`.

who.description: Author as the source names it; absent when the source names none.

at.description: Unix time of the original record; absent when the source has none.

kind.description: Media type of the original bytes.

text.description: The text the archive indexes, extracted by the connector.

LineType.description: `item`: an `Item`; `checkpoint`: every item before it may be considered stored at `cursor`; `done`: the run's last line, with the final cursor if it moved; `error`: the run's last line, an `Error`.

Line.description: One stdout line of a stdio connector: `type` with the fields of its variant inline, the `Item` fields for `item`, `cursor` for `checkpoint` and optionally `done`, the `Error` fields for `error`. The runner stores a cursor only after every item before it was answered.

who.description: `item`: author as the source names it.

at.description: `item`: Unix time of the original record.

kind.description: `item`: media type of the original bytes.

retry_after.description: `error` with `rate_limited`: seconds before the next run.

Page.description: The `structuredContent` of an MCP connector's `ulei_pull` result.

items.description: At most the request's `limit` items, in source order.

cursor.description: The position after these items, at most 4,096 bytes; null while the source gave none.

more.description: Whether the runner should call again with `cursor`.

ErrorCode.description: Why a run failed, and the runner's answer: `auth_failed` the source refused the key, `key_unreadable` the key file is missing or malformed, `source_unavailable` a network or source failure, each logged with the next run on schedule; `rate_limited` the source asked to wait, the next run not before `retry_after`; `bad_cursor` the stored cursor is not accepted, logged on every run until the owner's `reset`; `bad_request` the `Request` is not understood, `internal` anything else, both logged.

Error.description: A connector's failure: an `error` line without `type` (stdio) or the `structuredContent` of a result with `isError` (MCP).

retry_after.description: With `rate_limited`: seconds before the next run.

BrokerRequest.description: One line the connector writes on the broker socket, fd 3 named `broker`: a TCP connection to `connect`.

BrokerErrorCode.description: `not_allowed`: neither the manifest's `source.addresses` nor the owner's `allow` lists it, or it resolves to a loopback, private, link-local, unspecified or multicast address the owner did not allow; `resolve_failed`, `connect_failed`: no address resolved or connected within 10 s; `limit`: the run's 32 connections are used.

BrokerReply.description: The runner's answer line to a `BrokerRequest`: exactly one of `ok`, sent with the connected socket attached as `SCM_RIGHTS`, and `error`.

RunOutcome.description: How a run ended: `ok` with `done`; `error` with an `Error`; `timeout` past the manifest's `timeout`; `refused` before the connector started, by a missing key file or isolation; `exit` a non-zero exit without an `error` line; `protocol` a line that is not a valid `Line` or page; `archive` C10 failed or did not answer, with the cursor unchanged; `busy` due while its last run still ran, so not started.

Grants.description: The owner's records of `connectors.<name>` in effect for a run, each as `ulei.toml` gives it, lists split at commas; absent keys grant nothing.

read.description: More paths Landlock grants read on.

write.description: More paths Landlock grants write on.

network.description: `direct`: the run had its own sockets, not pinned to an address.

RunRecord.description: One line of `connectors.log` per run. It holds no item content and never a key's value.

at.description: Unix time the run started or was found busy or refused.

unit.description: The run's transient unit; absent when none was started.

code.description: The `ErrorCode` of an `error` outcome or the reason of a `refused` one; absent otherwise.

too_large.description: Items not sent because their `put` body would exceed 1,048,576 bytes.

too_large_ids.description: The `external_id` of every `too_large` item of the run, none dropped.

conflict_ids.description: The `external_id` of the first 16 `conflict` items of the run.

cursor_moved.description: Whether the run stored a new cursor.

landlock_abi.description: The Landlock ABI the run was restricted with; absent when it had none.

connect_ports.description: Under `network = "direct"`, the TCP ports Landlock let the run connect to: the ports of `source.addresses` and `allow`, ascending. Absent when its connect ports were not limited: without `direct`, below Landlock ABI 4 or under `landlock = "off"`.

stderr.description: The last 2,048 bytes of the connector's stderr, cut at a UTF-8 boundary.
